title: Comparative Constitutional Analysis: India vs UK, USA, France, Germany, Japan, Canada & Australia
article_tags: Due Process vs Procedure Established by Law

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: We adopted parliamentary democracy based on the British model, but how does our model differ from that model? 1. As regards legislation, the British Parliament is supreme or sovereign but in India, the power of the Parliament to legislate is limited. 2. In India, matters related to the constitutionality of the Amendment of an Act of the Parliament are referred to the Constitution Bench by the Supreme Court. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
relevant_prelims_pyqs.source_pdf: X-Factor Prelims- Indian Polity for Pre'2027.pdf

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: A Parliamentary System of Government is one in which

options.a: all political parties in the Parliament are represented in the Government
options.b: the Government is responsible to the Parliament and can be removed by it
options.c: the Government is elected by the people and can be removed by them
options.d: the Government is chosen by the Parliament but cannot be removed by it before completion of a fixed term

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: Out of the following statements, choose the one that brings out the principle underlying the Cabinet form of Government :

options.a: An arrangement for minimizing the criticism against the Government whose responsibilities are complex and hard to carry out to the satisfaction of all.
options.b: A mechanism for speeding up the activities of the Government whose responsibilities are increasing day by day.
options.c: A mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people.
options.d: A device for strengthening the hands of the head of the Government whose hold over the people is in a state of decline.

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: The main advantage of the parliamentary form of government is that

options.a: the executive and legislature work independently.
options.b: it provides continuity of policy and is more efficient.
options.c: the executive remains responsible to the legislature.
options.d: the head of the government cannot be changed without election.

options.a: Lok Sabha is elected directly by the people
options.d: Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha

relevant_mains_pyqs.question_text: Examine how the separation of powers is practised in India compared to the rigid presidential model of the United States of America. In this context, compare the actual authority of the Indian Prime Minister with that of the President of the USA. (15)
Compare and contrast the President's power to pardon in India and in the USA. Are there any limits to it in both countries? What are 'preemptive pardons'? (10)
Discuss India as a secular state and compare it with the secular principles of the US constitution. (15)
Compare and contrast the British and Indian approaches to Parliamentary sovereignty. 10
Critically examine the procedures through which the Presidents of India and France are elected. (15)
Analyze the distinguishing features of the notion of Equality in the Constitutions of the USA and India. (15)

The judicial systems in India and UK seem to be converging as well as diverging in recent times. Highlight the key points of convergence and divergence between the two nations in terms of their judicial practices. (10)
What can France learn from the Indian Constitution's approach to secularism? (10)
Indian and USA are two large democracies. Examine the basic tenets on which the two political systems are based. (15)
